notes: deleteWorldSlot compares the target slot's id against WorldSlotManager.resolvedActiveSlotID (line 301) before calling the pure WorldSlotManager.deleteSlot at all -- the guard lives in the orchestration layer, not the file-system layer, matching the pattern every other destructive slot operation uses (running-server guards live in AppViewModel, not WorldSlotManager). The underlying WorldSlotManager.deleteSlot (line 795) has no awareness of 'active' and would happily remove any directory it's given; Phase 6's application service must reproduce this same active-slot refusal at the same layer, not rely on the repository to enforce it.
